original_query: SELECT t0.JOB FROM (SELECT EMPNO, ENAME, JOB, MGR, HIREDATE, SAL, COMM, DEPTNO, SLACKER, DEPTNO + EMPNO AS f9 FROM EMP WHERE ENAME = 'A') AS t0 FULL JOIN (SELECT DEPTNO, NAME, DEPTNO + 5 AS f2 FROM DEPT) AS t1 ON t0.JOB = t1.NAME AND t0.f9 = t1.f2 GROUP BY t0.JOB
rewritten_query:
WITH emp_a AS (
    SELECT job, deptno + empno AS f9
    FROM emp
    WHERE ename = 'A'
)
SELECT job
FROM emp_a
UNION
SELECT NULL
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM dept d
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM emp_a e
        WHERE e.job = d.name
          AND e.f9 = d.deptno + 5
    )
)

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Inline the derived tables t0 and t1 since they are simple projections of EMP and DEPT with no aggregation or deduplication, allowing the optimizer to fuse filters and joins directly.
Push the ENAME = 'A' filter directly onto the EMP base table before the FULL JOIN to reduce the join input early.

The FULL JOIN followed by GROUP BY t0.JOB means DEPT-only rows only contribute a NULL group. The query can be rewritten as a UNION of distinct JOB values from filtered EMP plus a single NULL when any DEPT row is unmatched, replacing the expensive FULL JOIN with an anti-join (NOT EXISTS).
Replace the FULL JOIN against all 450K DEPT rows with an anti-join on the small filtered EMP set to avoid hashing/scanning the entire DEPT table just to produce a NULL group.
The expressions DEPTNO + EMPNO and DEPTNO + 5 are computed in the derived tables; keep them once in the CTE so they are evaluated only on the filtered rows.
